Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Radium discovered?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
In what year was Copper discovered?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
Mil Mi-17: Kazan Helicopters. It is known as the Mi-8M series in Russian service.
In which country is Minamata disease?
Minamata disease: Japan. Minamata disease (Japanese: 水俣病, Hepburn: Minamata-byō) is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning.
Who is credited with discovering Thorium?
Thorium: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Thorium is a chemical element; it has symbol Th and atomic number 90.
Who is credited with discovering Cauchy–Schwarz inequality?
Cauchy–Schwarz inequality: Viktor Bunyakovsky. It is considered one of the most important and widely used inequalities in mathematics.
Who is credited with discovering Phosphorus?
Phosphorus: Hennig Brand. Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Formed by the angle of thyroid cartilage around the voice box, this neck protrusion becomes a prominent secondary sex characteristic in most men during puberty — what is it commonly called?
Adam's apple is the protrusion in the neck formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage surrounding the larynx, typically visible in men and less so in women.
Given by mouth, IV, or directly into bone marrow, which antiarrhythmic medication treats conditions like ventricular tachycardia but risks serious lung and thyroid side effects?
Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication used to treat and prevent a number of types of cardiac dysrhythmias.
This emotion is defined by dread over events that haven't happened yet, distinguishing it from fear, which responds to a threat that's already present. What is it?
Anxiety is an emotion characterized by an unpleasant state of inner turmoil and includes feelings of dread over anticipated events.
These large Old World monkeys come in six distinct species, each native to a different region of Africa, with one species also found on the Arabian Peninsula — what primate is it?
Baboon are primates comprising the genus Papio, one of the 23 genera of Old World monkeys, in the family Cercopithecidae.
First coined in 1919 by Hungarian engineer Károly Ereky, this multidisciplinary field harnesses living organisms like bacteria and yeast to make products and services. What field is it?

Biotechnology is a multidisciplinary field that involves the integration of natural sciences and engineering sciences to achieve the application of organisms and parts thereof for products and services.

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered in 1962 while still a Cambridge Ph.D. student — then later turned, controversially, to Transcendental Meditation. Which physicist is he?
Brian Josephson (born 4 January 1940) is a British theoretical physicist and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge.
Bordered by Aquila, Sagittarius, and Aquarius in the sky's watery region, this half-goat, half-fish zodiac figure is the tiniest of the twelve — which constellation?
Capricornus is one of the constellations of the zodiac.
Known as garbanzo, chana or Bengal gram, this protein-rich legume is mashed into hummus and fried into falafel, with its oldest remains found in Syria — what is it?
Chickpea (Cicer arietinum) is an annual legume of the family Fabaceae, subfamily Faboideae, cultivated for its edible seeds.
More closely related to lungfish and land vertebrates than to ordinary ray-finned fish, this ancient lobe-finned fish survives today as a single genus with just two known species — which fish?
Coelacanth are an ancient group of lobe-finned fish (Sarcopterygii) in the class Actinistia.

This interdisciplinary field, whose name combines a Latin word for 'accusation' with a Greek suffix meaning 'study of,' draws on sociology, psychology, economics, and law to examine crime and deviant behavior. What field is this?
Criminology (from Latin crimen, 'accusation', and Ancient Greek -, -logia, from logos, 'word, reason') is the interdisciplinary study of crime and deviant behaviour.
This annual herb in the celery family, native to North Africa and West Asia, is grown across Eurasia for both its feathery leaves and its seeds, both used to flavor food — what herb is it?
Dill (Anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family Apiaceae.

Distinguished by permanently erect front fangs and a habit of rearing up while flaring a neck flap, which family of mostly venomous snakes ranges from an 18 cm white-lipped species to a nearly 6-metre giant?
Elapidae (commonly known as elapids, from Ancient) is a family of snakes characterized by their permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth.

This genus of 700-plus flowering trees gets its name from Greek words meaning 'well covered' — a nod to the little cap fused over its stamens — and most species are native to Australia. The leafy 'gum trees' in question are which?
Eucalyptus is a genus of more than 700 species of flowering plants in the family Myrtaceae.
Found at the terminal end of the limb in many vertebrates, this weight-bearing anatomical structure enables locomotion and is typically made up of multiple bony segments — what is it?
Foot (pl.: feet) is an anatomical structure found in many vertebrates. The plural form feet is an instance of i-mutation.

Sometimes called the 'lesser apes' to distinguish them from chimpanzees, gorillas, and orangutans, these smaller, tailless primates live in forests from eastern Bangladesh through Southeast Asia and don't build nests — what are they?
Gibbon are apes in the family Hylobatidae (hylobatids).
This flatfish's English name blends words for 'holy' and 'flat fish,' a nod to its place on the Catholic holy-day menu. Which bottom-dwelling fish?
Halibut is the common name for three species of flatfish in the family of right-eye flounders.
Nesting monogamously in tree cavities across Africa, Asia, and Melanesia, these birds are unique for having their first two neck vertebrae fused solid — which birds?
Hornbill are birds found in tropical and subtropical Africa, Asia and Melanesia of the family Bucerotidae.

Co-creator of the breakthrough neural network AlexNet and a contributor to landmark AI systems including GPT and AlphaGo, this computer scientist has won a major deep-learning research award three years running — who is he?
Ilya Sutskever (born 1986) is a computer scientist who specializes in machine learning.
This American psychiatrist and Communist Party USA member is best remembered today for her romantic relationship with J. Robert Oppenheimer — who was she?
Jean Tatlock (February 21, 1914 - January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
Drawing on physiology, biomechanics, and neuropsychology, this scientific discipline studies human body movement and underpins fields from sports psychology to physical therapy — what is it?
Kinesiology (from Ancient Greek (knsis) 'movement' and - -loga 'study of') is the scientific study of human body movement.
This German-born American businessman founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans, launching his San Francisco firm in 1853 — who is he?
Levi Strauss (STROWSS; born Lb Strau,; February 26, 1829 - September 26, 1902) was a German-born American businessman who founded the first company to manufacture blue jeans.
The sole species in its genus, this South Chinese fruit has a sweet, mildly tart flavor and a distinctive rose-like floral aroma — name it?
Lychee (US also) are the fruit of the tree Litchi chinensis, the sole member of the genus Litchi, part of the soapberry family, Sapindaceae.
This genus of flowering plants belongs to the chamomile tribe of the sunflower family, and several of its species go by the folk name 'mayweed' — which genus?
Matricaria is a genus of flowering plants in the chamomile tribe within the sunflower family.
Touch this creeping legume's compound leaves and they fold inward within seconds, only reopening minutes later — a textbook example of rapid plant movement. What plant is it?

Mimosa pudica (also called sensitive plant, sleepy grass, sleepy plant, action plant, humble plant, touch-me-not, touch-and-die, shame plant or shy plant) is a creeping annual or perennial flowering plant of the pea/legume family Fabaceae.
Developed under a hypersonic flight program in the late 1990s, three single-use examples of this scramjet aircraft were built, the first destroyed in a 2001 test flight — which record holder is it?
NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Built from proteins, DNA, and RNA around specific chromosomal regions, this nuclear structure is being studied as a target for cancer chemotherapy — what is it?
Nucleolus (pl.: nucleoli) is the largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
Founded as a science by Georges Cuvier in 1796, when he demonstrated evidence for extinction, this field studies prehistoric life mainly through fossils — what's the discipline?
Paleontology is the scientific study of the life of the past, mainly but not exclusively through the study of fossils.
Which management theorist and educator's writings on organizing business, government, and nonprofit sectors made him one of the most influential thinkers on modern management?

Peter Drucker (November 19, 1909 - November 11, 2005) was an Austrian American management consultant, educator, and author, whose writings contributed to the philosophical and practical foundations of modern management theory.
This genus of single-celled parasites moves from mosquito to human bloodstream, destroying red blood cells and causing a disease with recurring fevers — what is this genus called?
Plasmodium is a genus of unicellular eukaryotes that are obligate parasites of vertebrates and insects.
Classified into acute, chronic, and pelvic pain syndrome subtypes, this condition doesn't always match its name's literal meaning of organ swelling — which condition?
Prostatitis is an umbrella term for a variety of medical conditions that incorporate bacterial and non-bacterial origin illnesses in the pelvic region.

This bird of prey now breeds only in Europe, though it once also ranged across West Asia and Northwest Africa, with northern populations historically wintering as far as western Africa — what bird is it?
Red kite (Milvus milvus) is a bird of prey in the family Accipitridae, which also includes many other diurnal raptors such as eagles, buzzards, and harriers.
This root vegetable — a hybrid of cabbage and a related turnip-like plant — goes by different names in North America and Britain, and is often confused for a big turnip. What is it?
Rutabaga (North American English) or swede (British English and some Commonwealth English) is a root vegetable, a form of Brassica napus (which also includes rapeseed).
This Soviet rocket engineer led the early development of his country's space program and designed the R-7, the world's first intercontinental ballistic missile — who is he?
Sergei Korolev was Soviet aerospace engineer (1907–1966).

Barred from a formal education, she learned mathematics from her father's library and wrote to Gauss under the male pseudonym 'Monsieur Le Blanc,' later winning a Paris Academy prize for her work on elasticity. Which French mathematician was she?
Sophie Germain (1 April 1776 - 27 June 1831) was a French mathematician, physicist, and philosopher.
Developed from an earlier design, this variable-sweep-wing Soviet fighter-bomber served from 1967 to 1990 and was exported in variants like the Su-22 — which aircraft is it?
Sukhoi Su-17 (NATO reporting name: Fitter) is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military.
A metabolite of caffeine processed in the liver, this bitter alkaloid is the main one in the cacao plant and turns up in chocolate, tea, and kola nuts. What is it?
Theobromine is the principal alkaloid of Theobroma cacao (cacao plant).
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
Its wild form is dioecious while domesticated versions bear hermaphrodite flowers — this Mediterranean-native plant is the ancestor of nearly all wine and table varieties — what species?

Vitis vinifera is a species of flowering plant, native to the Mediterranean region, Central Europe, and southwestern Asia, from Morocco and Portugal north to southern Germany and east to northern Iran.
Which East Asian citrus fruit, believed to have originated in central China as a hybrid of mandarin orange and ichang papeda, is now also grown in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe?
Yuzu (Citrus junos, from Japanese or) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
Nicknamed the 'upside-down tree' for its unusual silhouette, this genus of long-lived African and Malagasy giants was named after a French naturalist — what genus is it?
Adansonia: Genus of trees known as baobab.
Made in the adrenal cortex, this hormone tells the kidney to hang onto sodium and dump potassium, quietly steering your blood pressure and blood volume — what is it?
Formed when ammonia gains an extra hydrogen ion, this positively charged molecule, NH4+, is a key player in the global nitrogen cycle — what is it?
This scientific practice of systematically measuring the human body has been used in paleoanthropology, historical living-standards research, and modern clothing design — what is it called?
Anthropometry: Measurement of the human individual.

This umbrella term for joint disease covers conditions like osteoarthritis, most common in weight-bearing joints as people age, and the autoimmune form that typically targets the hands and feet. What condition is this?
Best known for pioneering radical behaviorism at Harvard, this psychologist invented a chamber for studying operant conditioning that came to bear his name — who is he?
B. F. Skinner: American psychologist and social philosopher (1904–1990)

This Swiss-American engineer was the only one of a famous physicist's three known biological grandsons to survive childhood, and later earned patents in electronics while working at Texas Instruments — who was he?

Developed to supplement the 727 on short routes, this narrow-body twinjet kept the 707's fuselage width and six-abreast seating and entered service with Lufthansa in 1968 — which best-selling aircraft is it?
Patented by Roche in 1961 and approved for medical use in 1974, which benzodiazepine, similar in effect to diazepam, is sometimes given as a presurgical sedative in 1.5, 3, or 6 mg tablets?
Bromazepam: Benzodiazepine drug. Bromazepam, sold under many brand names, is a benzodiazepine.
First synthesized in 1950 by bombarding curium with alpha particles, this actinide element bears the symbol Cf and is named for a US university and state — what is it?
Californium: Chemical element with atomic number 98 (Cf)
This corvid, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic, is stockier and larger than its North American cousin but nearly identical in appearance — what bird is it?
Carrion crow: Species of bird. The carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Often called 'the father of the computer,' this English polymath designed the difference engine and the analytical engine, borrowing a punch-card principle from the Jacquard loom — who is he?
Charles Babbage: English mathematician, philosopher, and engineer (1791–1871)
One of the original citrus fruits, this large fragrant relative of the lemon has a thick, coarse rind and is a genetic ancestor of most modern citrus hybrids — what is it?

A member of the true thrushes, this Eurasian songbird whose nominate male is all black breeds across Europe, western Asia, and North Africa and has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand — which bird is it?
Common blackbird: Thrush native to Europe, western Asia and North Africa.
Also nicknamed the prairie wolf, this adaptable North American canine fills a similar ecological niche to Eurasia's golden jackal and was first spotted in Panama in 2013 — what is it?
Coyote: Species of canine native to North America.

Affecting about half of all adults and often treated with antifungal cream, this common scalp condition causes flaking and mild itchiness but isn't actually caused by poor hygiene. What condition is it?
Dandruff: Skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.

Driven by a gradient in chemical potential, this stochastic process describes the net movement of particles from areas of higher to lower concentration and can even reverse direction in spinodal decomposition — what physical process is this?
Diffusion: Transport of dissolved species from the highest to the lowest concentration region.
Defined in humans as an adult height of four foot ten or shorter, this condition's most common form — accounting for about 70% of cases — is a genetic disorder called achondroplasia. What is it?
Dwarfism: Small size of an organism, caused by growth deficiency or genetic mutations.
This stage of development begins right after fertilization, progressing from a single-celled zygote through a ball of cells called a morula — what is it called?
Embryo: Multicellular diploid eukaryote in its earliest stage of development.
This white solid is prized for binding iron and calcium ions into water-soluble complexes — handy for dissolving scale — and goes by a four-letter acronym. What is it?
In this common vision condition, distant objects appear sharp but close-up objects blur because light focuses behind the retina instead of on it - what is it?
Farsightedness: Eye condition in which light is focused behind instead of on the retina.
Sold under the brand name Luvox, this SSRI antidepressant treats OCD and other anxiety disorders, with milder side effects than most in its class except gastrointestinal ones — what drug is it?
Fluvoxamine: SSRI antidepressant. Fluvoxamine, sold under the brand name Luvox among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
Capable of living up to 177 years and weighing as much as 417 kilograms, which giant reptile — native to a chain of Pacific islands named for it — is the largest cold-blooded land animal alive today?
Galápagos tortoise: Species of reptile. The species comprises 15 subspecies (12 extant and 3 extinct).
Named from a Latin word for sword, this genus of cormous flowering plants in the iris family is sometimes called the 'sword lily' and is most diverse in South Africa's Cape region — which genus?
Gladiolus: Genus of perennial flowering plants. It is sometimes called the 'sword lily', but is usually called by its generic name (plural gladioli).

Once classified as a subfamily of the seabasses, this diverse family of marine ray-finned fish is now treated as distinct, with most members drawn from two large genera. What are they commonly called?
Grouper: Family of fishes. The common name "grouper" is usually given to fish in one of two large genera: Epinephelus and Mycteroperca.
About the size of a closed fist and enclosed in a protective sac called the pericardium, this four-chambered organ sits in the chest between the lungs and pumps blood through the body — which organ?
Heart: Organ found in humans and other animals.
This genus of over 570 flowering plants — the only living genus in its family — includes the evergreen shrub famous for Christmas decorations and cards. What genus is it?
Holly: Genus of flowering plants. Ilex or holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.

This neurological disorder involves excessive sleepiness or time spent sleeping, sometimes linked to seasonal affective disorder, and appears under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5 — what is it called?

Hypersomnia: Neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness. It can have many possible causes (such as seasonal affective disorder) and can cause distress and problems with functioning.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
This fragrant genus of shrubs and vines in the olive family is grown in vast quantities in one Egyptian village that supplies much of the world's perfume industry — which plant?
Jasmine: Genus of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae.
Born Giulia Maddalena Angela in Italy, this physician became a leading freethinker and activist for women's rights and social reform in early-20th-century Argentina — who is she?
Julieta Lanteri: Argentine doctor and activist (1873–1932)
Nocturnal, owl-faced, and unable to fly, this endangered New Zealand bird holds the title of the world's heaviest parrot. What is it?
Kākāpō: Parrot endemic to New Zealand. It is the only parrot to have a polygynous lek breeding system.
This synthetic thyroid hormone treats hypothyroidism, has a half-life of roughly 7.5 days, and is not intended for weight loss — what's this medication?
Levothyroxine: Thyroid hormone medication. Levothyroxine, also known as L-thyroxine, is a synthetic form of the thyroid hormone thyroxine (T4).
Sold as Ativan, this benzodiazepine treats anxiety, insomnia, and active seizures, and is even used during surgery to interfere with memory formation — what medication is it?
Lorazepam: Benzodiazepine medication. Lorazepam, sold under the brand name Ativan among others, is a benzodiazepine medication.
Produced when beta-amylase breaks starch down two glucose units at a time, which reducing disaccharide gets its name from the germinating-seed process of malting?
Grown from the YF-17 that lost the Air Force's lightweight fighter contest, which twin-engine carrier jet won a second life when the Navy picked it instead?
McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet: American carrier-capable multirole strike aircraft.
A physician-turned-hedge-fund-manager, this investor famously predicted the subprime mortgage crisis and was portrayed in the 2015 film The Big Short — who is he?
Michael Burry: American hedge fund manager (born 1971)
Nicknamed 'water warts,' this viral skin infection causes small pink bumps with a telltale dimple in the center and usually clears up on its own within a year — what is it?

Molluscum contagiosum: Viral infection of the skin. Molluscum contagiosum (MC), sometimes called water warts, is a viral infection of the skin that results in small raised pink lesions with a dimple in the center.
This lipid-rich substance wraps around nerve axons in segments, leaving gaps called nodes of Ranvier that let electrical signals leap along in a process called saltatory conduction — what is it?
Myelin: Fatty substance insulating nerve cell axons.

This silvery-white transition metal with a faint golden tinge resists corrosion thanks to a thin oxide layer, and in pure native form it's mostly found inside iron meteorites — which element, atomic number 28, is it?
Nickel: Chemical element with atomic number 28 (Ni)
This soft-bodied mollusc can radically deform its shape to squeeze through tiny gaps and propels itself backward by jetting water through a siphon — what eight-limbed creature is it?
Octopus: Soft-bodied eight-limbed order of molluscs.
Sold under the brand name Anavar, this synthetic anabolic steroid helps burn victims and Turner syndrome patients gain weight — what is it?
Oxandrolone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It was sold under the brand names Oxandrin and Anavar, among others.
First domesticated in Neolithic China, this tree's fruit comes in a fuzzy form and a glossy-skinned twin called the nectarine — what fruit, a rose-family relative of the cherry and plum?
Peach: Type of fruit tree, or its fruit.
The body produces about a quart of this substance daily to trap airborne particles and bacteria — coughed up, it's also known as sputum. What is it?
Phlegm: Mucus produced by the respiratory system (excluding the nasal passages)
Commonly called frangipani, this fragrant flowering shrub native to Mexico and the Caribbean is now a beloved ornamental in Hawaii and desert climates of Arabia — what genus is it?
Plumeria: Genus of flowering plants endemic to the Americas.
Defined as supervising a team to hit all its goals within three primary constraints — scope, time, and budget — what is this discipline?
Project management: Practice of leading the work of a team to achieve goals and criteria at a specified time.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes — including some of the world's largest — must coil around prey and squeeze it into cardiac arrest before swallowing it whole. What is the family?
Pythonidae: Family of snakes. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.

Nicknamed 'the Thud' by its crews, this Mach 2 jet flew most of the early Vietnam War's strike missions and became the only American aircraft ever pulled from combat over unsustainable losses — which plane?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief: US Air Force supersonic fighter-bomber.
Native to tropical Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this medium-sized parrot has established wild populations worldwide after pet-trade escapees adapted brilliantly to city life — which bird?

Rose-ringed parakeet: Species of bird. The rose-ringed parakeet (Psittacula krameri), also known as the ring-necked parakeet, is a medium-sized parrot in the genus Psittacula, of the family Psittaculidae.
This Sapporo-born programmer rose to become Nintendo's fourth president, betting on novel, entertaining games over the most powerful hardware — who is he?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Satoru Iwata: Japanese video game executive (1959–2015)
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Native to Southern Europe and Anatolia, this deciduous tree produces an edible nut that's been used in cooking since ancient times — what is it commonly called?
Sweet chestnut: Species of tree. A substantial, long-lived deciduous tree, it produces an edible seed, the chestnut, which has been used in cooking since ancient times.
An Australian-American math prodigy who won the Fields Medal in 2006, he proved a famous theorem on prime numbers with Ben Green in 2004. Who is he?
Terence Tao: Australian and American mathematician (born 1975)

Proposing an information-management system in March 1989, this English computer scientist implemented the first web browser and web server and founded the organization that still oversees the web's standards — who is he?

Endemic to New Zealand and often mistaken for a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that thrived back in the Mesozoic era — its Māori name means 'peaks on the back.' What is it?
Tuatara: Species of reptile. The tuatara (Māori: [ˈtʉ.a.ta.ɾa]; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This glycopeptide antibiotic is given intravenously for MRSA infections like endocarditis and meningitis, but taken orally - where it's poorly absorbed - to treat a common gut infection - which drug?
Vancomycin: Antibiotic medication. Vancomycin is also taken orally (by mouth) to treat Clostridioides difficile infections.
Recognized by their unusually long snouts, these small herbivorous beetles number around 97,000 species and include notorious crop pests that damage stored grain — what are they called?
Weevil: Superfamily of beetles. It also includes bark beetles, which while morphologically dissimilar to other weevils in lacking the distinctive snout, is a subfamily of Curculionidae.
With atomic number 39, this silvery metal is chemically similar to the lanthanides, never occurs freely in nature, and once gave old CRT televisions their red phosphor glow — which element?
Yttrium: Chemical element with atomic number 39 (Y)
What is the chemical symbol for rhodium?
The symbol for rhodium is Rh. Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
What is the chemical symbol for indium?
The symbol for indium is In. Indium is a chemical element; its symbol is In and its atomic number is 49.

In what year was Steve McQueen born?
Steve McQueen: Terrence Stephen McQueen (March 24, 1930 – November 7, 1980) was an American actor.
In what year was Matt Damon born?
Matt Damon: Matthew Paige Damon (DAY-mən; born October 8, 1970) is an American actor, film producer, and screenwriter.
In what year was Brendan Fraser born?
Brendan Fraser: Brendan James Fraser ( FRAY-zər; born December 3, 1968) is an American and Canadian actor.
In what year was Rosario Dawson born?
Rosario Dawson: Rosario Isabel Dawson (born May 9, 1979) is an American actress and activist.
In what year was George Clooney born?
George Clooney: George Timothy Clooney (born May 6, 1961) is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Michael Sheen born?
Michael Sheen: Michael Christopher Sheen (born 5 February 1969) is a Welsh actor.
In what year was Mahershala Ali born?
Mahershala Ali ( mə-HUR-shə-lə; born Mahershalalhashbaz Gilmore on February 16, 1974) is an American actor.
In what year was Jessica Alba born?
Jessica Alba: Jessica Marie Alba ( AL-bə; born April 28, 1981) is an American actress and businesswoman.
In what year was Jacob Elordi born?
Jacob Elordi: Jacob Nathaniel Elordi (born 26 June 1997) is an Australian actor.
In what year was Cate Blanchett born?
Cate Blanchett: Catherine Élise Blanchett ( BLAN-chit; born 14 May 1969) is an Australian actor and producer.
In what year did Howard Hughes die?
Howard Hughes: Howard Robard Hughes Jr. (December 24, 1905 – April 5, 1976) was an American aviator, aerospace engineer, business magnate, film producer, and investor.
In what year did Alfred Hitchcock die?
